thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Elevated 5xx rate detected in prod-us-west (gateway errors + timeouts). Severity: P1. Metric link: https://metrics.redwood.internal/d/alerts/5xx-spike

sara (oncall): I'm paged, starting triage. Noticing error rate jumps at 17:12 UTC. Correlating with prefix-kv cache metrics.

james (infra): seeing huge eviction delta on prefix cache shards. eviction_rate per-shard spiked ~x40 around 17:10. Also saw sudden VM memory pressure from a single host pool.

maria (runtime): logs show repeated "prefix_cache_miss -> backend_read" churn and an uptick in request latencies hitting the gateway which then surfaces 502/504. Suspect eviction storm => thundering herd.

leo (sre): customer ops: ~12 customers reported API 5xx in last 8 minutes, mostly read-heavy endpoints. Status page draft: "We are investigating elevated errors in US-West. Some requests may return 5xx or timeouts. Mitigations in progress."

sara (oncall): quick snapshot of relevant metrics (copying from dashboards):
```
prefix_cache_evictions: 75231/s (normal ~1800/s)
prefix_cache_miss_ratio: 0.84 -> 0.12 before spike
prefix_cache_fill_latency: 120ms -> 850ms
gateway_5xx_rate: 6.8% -> 0.9% baseline
backend_read_latency_p50: 30ms -> 420ms
```

james (infra): initial hypothesis: a misbehaving rollout or bad traffic pattern caused cache thrash; eviction loop leads to more backend reads which crowds the I/O layer. Also noticed one node in pool-a restarted an agent process ~17:05 and then rejoined; could be hot-shard causing skew.

maria (runtime): mitigation options — choose one or more:
- temporarily disable prefix caching for the top-traffic keyspaces (safest, immediate).
- increase cache retention / bump memory on a subset (riskier, slower).
- enable traffic-shedding / rate-limiting at gateway for non-critical routes.
- route heavy customers to dedicated path or fallback variant (if available).

sara (oncall): recommend: 1) flip cache-bypass header for read endpoints (non-destructive) 2) add a soft rate limit for the problematic route 3) open a canary to confirm.

james (infra): running canary change to inject header for 5% of traffic to bypass prefix cache. Command:
```
# release canary to route config (infra-control)
infractl route update --service gateway-prod --route /v1/embeds --set header:REDWOOD_CACHE_BYPASS=1 --canary 5%
```

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Canary deploy triggered: canary_id=canary-2156001. Monitoring metrics for 5 minutes.

maria (runtime): while canary warms up, I'm preparing a script to clear the hot prefix shard keys from the in-memory cache on the affected nodes. This will avoid mass eviction. Script: `scripts/eviction_quarantine.sh --shard=prefix-42 --rate=1000`

leo (sre): ops-bot ran an automated quick-fix: increased soft-cache TTL for prefix-42 on nodes 3-6. ops-bot: "applied ttl bump, watching for OOM"

ops-bot: Logs: "ttl_bump(prefix-42) applied on nodes [3,4,5,6], new_ttl=45s"

sara (oncall): early canary results: bypassed traffic shows 5xx rate back down to baseline for those requests. Gateway CPU for canary hosts lower by ~18%. Good signal.

james (infra): rolling canary to 25% then 60% with careful watch. Commands executed.

maria (runtime): while rolling, I'm disabling prefix prefetch for the affected keyspace to reduce background churn: `runtimectl config set prefix_prefetch:false --keyspace customers-heavy`

sara (oncall): customer impact update: 12 customers reported; now down to 3 with intermittent errors. Posting to status page: "Mitigation in progress; partial relief observed for some customers after temporary routing changes."

leo (sre): observed one backend storage node showing increased IO wait. James, can you check disk IO rates and whether we need to throttle read-through concurrency?

james (infra): checked: io_ops spiked on storage-b-2, concurrent reads ~4x. Throttling read concurrency at gateway in flight limit = 80 -> 30 for that route to protect storage. Command: `infractl limit set --route /v1/embeds --inflight 30`

maria (runtime): logs after throttling + bypass:
```
2026-03-15T17:28:45Z prefix-evictor[5]: evict_rate=2100/s
2026-03-15T17:28:46Z gateway[2]: 5xx_rate=1.1%
2026-03-15T17:29:10Z storage-b-2: io_wait=12% -> 3%
```

sara (oncall): good. Preparing handoff to daytime oncall (maria) in 17 minutes. I'll document actions taken and open a follow-up action item to look for root cause (rollout, key distribution, or memory leak).

maria (runtime): taking over. Summary I'm inheriting: prefix cache thrash caused by a hot-key churn after node restart + aggressive prefetch; mitigations applied: cache-bypass header rolled to ~60%, soft TTL bump on hot shards, prefetch disabled for heavy keyspace, gateway inflight limit reduced, targeted cache clear on 4 nodes. Monitoring shows 5xx back to ~0.6% and customer reports reduced.

sara (oncall): notes for postmortem: timeline, metrics, which nodes had restarts, exact config change IDs (infractl change ids), and a regression test for prefetch aggressiveness. Assign action items to infra + runtime.

james (infra): logging change ids: canary=canary-2156001, route-change-id=rc-77654, inflight-limit-change=lim-2156002, ttl-bump=cfg-2156003.

maria (runtime): I'll kick off an eval to replay the traffic pattern against a staging prefix cache with instrumented eviction metrics. Also will add a guard: if eviction_rate per shard > 5k/s, automatically cap prefetch and set bypass flag.

sara (oncall): thanks all. I'll close the P1 when metrics stable for 30m and update status page to "partial service restored; root cause investigation ongoing".

ops-bot: Incident P1 created: INC-2156004. Postmortem assigned to maria + james.

maria (runtime): taking postmortem. ping me if you see regression.

sara (oncall): handing off fully to maria at 17:40 UTC. Tagging incident channel for follow-up. :handshake:

james (infra): note — flagged an old host agent upgrade that coincided with the first restart; will include in postmortem.

leo (sre): customer ops updated status page to reflect mitigations and asked support to reach out to the 3 remaining impacted customers.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Status: mitigated -> monitoring. If 5xx_rate < 1% for 30m, incident will be resolved automatically.
